title: Scope resolution engine: precedence, merge by name/id, shadowing
description: at-engine::resolve builds the resolved item set from the four scope layers (Global, User, Project, Local). Precedence is nearest-wins: Local > Project > User > Global. Skills merge by normalized name (trim, NFC, case-insensitive compare, original spelling preserved for display); MCP servers merge by explicit `id` field, falling back to name when absent and recording that fallback. Every non-winning definition is reported as shadowed with ShadowedBy{scope,item_id,path}. Resolution is pure: it consumes ScopeSnapshot inputs and performs no IO.
acceptance: resolve() over 4 layers returns exactly one winning Definition per logical id; ordering is deterministic: kind, then name, then scope depth.
A skill defined as 'Code-Review' (User) and 'code-review' (Project) merges to one logical id with Project winning; no duplicate row.
Two MCP servers with the same name but different ids stay distinct; two with the same id merge and the loser is reported Shadowed{shadowed_by}.
An item defined at Global and Project yields one winner plus one Shadowed record carrying the losing path; removing the Project layer restores the Global winner with no code change.
Resolution of an empty snapshot returns an empty set, not an error.
notes: Skills name normalization must be shared with the add-skill clash check (TS slice) via at-model::normalized_name.

title: Global locks: persistence, propagation and denial reasons
description: A Lock pins an item to its Global definition. Implementation in at-engine::locks plus the locks table. A lock marks the resolved Definition Locked{reason,locked_at,locked_by_scope}. Any attempt to shadow, disable, edit or undeploy the item from a lower scope returns EngineError::Locked with the recorded reason. Lock/unlock is only accepted when the caller's active scope is Global.
acceptance: lock(item, reason) then resolve() marks the winner Locked and reports every deeper definition as Blocked{lock_id} instead of Shadowed.
disable_in_scope() and set_enabled() on a locked item return Err(Locked{reason}) and write zero bytes (verified by file hash before/after).
Unlocking from a lower scope returns Err(LockedAtGlobal) and leaves the lock row untouched.
Lock state is re-read from SQLite on every resolve call so a lock created by the CLI is visible in the open GUI without restart.
A lock pointing at a missing item yields an orphan-lock diagnostic in the lock list, not a panic.
notes: Locks live only in the `locks` table (TF-014); the Global store is not a lock source.

title: Disable-inherited tombstones in store.json
description: Disabling an inherited item for one scope writes a tombstone into that scope's store.json `disabled` array (decision 16: {item_id, kind, agents: [..] | null}), owned by TC-002 — never into mcp.json or a skills index. Tombstones are applied after precedence: the item is removed from the effective set for that scope and all deeper scopes, optionally only for the listed agents (null = all agents). Toggling back removes exactly the array element.
acceptance: disable(item, Project) writes one entry to .agentuna/store.json disabled[] with {item_id, kind, agents:null}; mcp.json and every skills file keep their pre-call hash.
A per-agent tombstone (agents:["codex"]) removes the item only from Codex's effective set; claude_code still loads it.
Re-enabling removes exactly the array element; the rest of store.json (schema_version, items[]) is byte-identical to before the disable.
Disabling an item locked at Global returns Err(Locked) with the lock reason and writes no store.json entry.
Duplicate tombstones for the same item/scope collapse to one row on load, and effective-config output exposes a DisabledHere row with tombstone scope and agents list.
notes: Decision 16: TC-002 owns the store.json schema; TA-003, TM-004 and TS-011 read/write the `disabled` key.

title: Local scope layer and gitignore handling
description: Local is the fourth real, writable scope (decision 4): machine-local overrides for all kinds, stored in <project>/.agentuna/local/ (gitignored, per decision 3) and rendered into agent-local files (.claude/settings.local.json and CLAUDE.local.md). AgenTuna writes .agentuna/local/ to the project .gitignore if absent and never offers to commit it.
acceptance: Local definitions win over Project for the same logical id; Effective config shows the Local badge and source path.

Local is writable for skills, MCP servers and rules: skills deploy to the adapter's project skills folder (decision 17), rules render to CLAUDE.local.md / .claude/settings.local.json, and every deployed Local path is added to .git/info/exclude exactly once.
ensure_gitignore() appends exactly one line '.agentuna/local/' and is a no-op when any equivalent pattern already exists.
Writing a Local item never resolves to a User or Global store path (path assertion in a unit test).
Local layer is skipped and flagged NotAvailable when the project is not a git repository, with the rest of resolution still working.
notes: Store layout is TC-owned per decision 3; TF-022 AppPaths resolves the local root; adapter stories own the per-agent project skills path.

title: Item state and sync-label derivation
description: at-engine::state computes ItemState (Linked, Off, Native, Conflict, Drifted) and SyncLabel (InSync, ProjectOnly, LibraryNewer, ProjectNewer) per (item, agent, scope) deployment by comparing store hash, deployed target hash and the last recorded baseline hash in item_versions. Native state means a real folder/entry exists that AgenTuna did not create. This is the only SyncLabel computation in the system; TC-015 reads and stores the result and never recomputes it (decision 12).
acceptance: State precedence is Conflict > Drifted > Native > Linked > Off, exercised by a table test with one row per transition.
A deployment whose store hash equals target hash and equals baseline is Linked + InSync; target hash differs from baseline with store unchanged is Drifted + ProjectNewer.
An unmanaged target folder with the same name as a store skill is Native, never Linked, and has no baseline row.
Missing target with a baseline row is Off + ProjectOnly; missing target with no baseline is Off.
Sync labels are produced here only: no other crate exposes a label derivation, and TC-015 consumes the value via the deployments row (assert single definition by a compile-fail/doc test).
notes: Decision 12: SyncLabel computed only in TA-005; TC-015 consumes it. Wording follows research/skillsmanager.md idea 4.

title: Effective config query API
description: One entry point, at-engine::effective::query(scope, agent_filter, kind_filter) -> EffectiveConfig, serving the Effective config screen, the per-agent file list and the CLI. It joins resolved definitions, deployments, tombstones and agent load counts, and returns for each row: logical id, kind, winner scope, source path, agents loading the item, state, and a 'loads_in_agents' count. Disabled rows are returned in a separate `disabled_here` vector.
acceptance: Query with kind=McpServers and agent=None returns one row per resolved server with agent_count equal to the number of installed agents whose config renders it.
Query with agent=Some(Codex) returns only servers Codex loads; servers with a disabled entry for Codex are absent from `items` and present in `disabled_here`.
Disabled rows carry reason and tombstone path; locked rows carry the lock id and reason.
Output is serde-serializable and the JSON produced for the CLI is byte-identical to the object the UI renders (same struct, one serializer).
Cold query on 500 items across 5 agents completes in < 200 ms on the test fixture; result is sorted by kind then display name.
notes: UI (TA-054) and CLI (TA-070) must consume this API, never recompute resolution.

title: Why-is-this-on trace builder
description: at-engine::why::trace(item_id, scope, agent) returns ordered TraceStep rows Global, User, Project, Local. Each step records presence (absent/defined/disabled/locked/shadowed/winning), file path, byte span and line number from the adapter's parsed document, a human-readable reason, and the agent-specific rendering path. A final Verdict states on/off plus the single decisive step.
acceptance: A server defined at User and inherited by Project produces 4 steps: User=Winning, Project=Inherited, Global=Absent, Local=Absent, with the User file path and 1-based line number.
A server disabled at Project produces Verdict off with decisive step Project=Disabled and the tombstone path; the User step stays Defined.
A server blocked by a Global lock produces the locked step with lock reason and no winning step.
Line numbers come from adapter-supplied spans (TM-005/006/007 for MCP, TA adapters for rules); a fixture with the server at line 42 reports 42 (golden test).
Trace performs no writes and works when the owning file is not readable, emitting StepStatus::Unreadable with the OS error string.
notes: Span data must come from adapters; do not grep files for line numbers.

title: Change-for-this-repo intents and ChangeSet planning
description: Three user intents from the Effective config screen: DisableInRepo (tombstone at Project or Local), OverrideInProject (copy the definition into ./.agentuna/ and let it shadow the inherited one), EditUserDefinition (no write, returns the owning scope so the UI navigates there). Each intent is planned into a ChangeSet of file operations with pre-rendered diffs; applying goes through at-fs with backup and concurrency checks.
acceptance: DisableInRepo emits exactly one op touching the project store tombstone file; the User/Global definition path never appears in the ChangeSet.
OverrideInProject emits a create op for the project definition plus a resolution re-run showing the new winner; the previous winner becomes Shadowed.
EditUserDefinition returns NavigateTo{scope,item} and an empty ChangeSet.
Any intent touching a locked item returns Err(Locked) with zero ops and the lock reason.
Every ChangeSet carries per-op diff text generated by `similar`, and applying it records one operations row with all touched files.
notes: Confirm dialogs are O09 (TU slice); this story is the engine side.

title: Overview aggregates: counts, needs-attention, recent changes
description: at-engine::overview::build(scope) produces the Overview payload: per-scope cards (skills/mcp/rules counts, lock count, last-edited timestamp), agents-on-this-Mac summary, needs-attention items and the recent-changes feed (last 20 operations). Needs attention aggregates: failing health checks, shadowed items, drift events, missing agents, native items outside AgenTuna. Each entry carries severity, title, subtitle and a NavigationTarget so the UI can jump to the exact screen/row.
acceptance: Empty store returns 3 scope cards with zero counts, empty needs_attention and empty recent_changes, no error.
Counts for the Project scope exclude items shadowed by Local and include tombstones only in a separate `disabled_count`.
needs_attention emits one row per distinct problem class per item, ordered Critical > Warning > Info, capped at 5 per class with a total count retained.
recent_changes returns operations ordered by created_at desc, each with operation id, summary, relative time and touched file count, limited to 20.
last_edited is null when a scope has no store, and the card renders as 'Not set up' rather than epoch zero.
notes: Payload is the single source for F03 and the CLI overview command.

title: Rule file discovery across scopes and agents
description: at-engine::rules::scan discovers instruction files per scope and per agent using verified adapter paths, not hard-coded names: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.local.md (any case), Cursor .cursor/rules/*.mdc, Codex ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, plus project <root>/CLAUDE.md and <root>/AGENTS.md. Each file becomes a RuleSource{scope, agent_consumers, path, bytes, mtime, sha256, managed:bool, link_target}. Broken symlinks and unreadable files are reported as diagnostics without aborting the scan.
acceptance: On a temp HOME fixture with CLAUDE.md only at project root, scan returns one RuleSource with scope=Project and agent_consumers=[ClaudeCode].
A file named claude.md (lowercase) is discovered on macOS and reported with its actual on-disk name.
A symlinked rule file is recorded with link_target; a dangling symlink yields Diagnostic::BrokenSymlink and no RuleSource.
An unreadable file (chmod 000) yields Diagnostic::PermissionDenied for that path while other files are still returned.
Two scans without file changes produce identical results and no duplicate DB rows (upsert key scope+path).
notes: Discovery is agent-path driven so a custom agent can declare its own rule file names.

title: One rule source rendered into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md
description: AgenTuna keeps a canonical rule source (rules/AGENTS.md in the store) and renders it into both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md at the same scope. Each target file is edited only inside a managed block delimited by <!-- agentuna:begin --> ... <!-- agentuna:end -->; content outside the block is preserved byte for byte. Render is deterministic and idempotent, and refuses to operate when the block markers are missing from a file AgenTuna claims to own or unterminated.
acceptance: Editing the source once produces two file writes whose managed-block content is identical; a second render writes nothing (byte-identical, no mtime change).
Existing user text above and below the managed block survives verbatim; the diff touches only lines inside the block.
A target file with an unterminated managed block returns Err(MalformedManagedBlock{path,line}) and writes neither file.
If a target exists but has no AgenTuna markers, the first render returns Err(AdoptRequired{path}) and performs no write.
Both resulting files are recorded in item_versions with their hashes and one operations row is written for the pair.
notes: Managed-block markers are AgenTuna's own; never rewrite a file Claude Code or Codex owns wholesale.

title: Rule editor save path with concurrency and conflict detection
description: Saving an edited rule goes through TA-011's managed-block renderer: the editor buffer is the content that replaces the managed block, never a whole-file rewrite of hand-authored text. Save rechecks the read-on-open hash and mtime before the atomic rename, takes a backup, updates item_versions and the operations log, and suppresses the resulting self-write event in the watcher. Edits that would touch bytes inside the AgenTuna markers by hand are refused (decision 13). A changed hash or mtime since open returns Err(Conflict) carrying a unified diff of disk vs editor buffer.
acceptance: Save of an unchanged buffer is a no-op (Saved{changed:false}, no new backup, no operations row).

Save replaces only the managed block; text outside <!-- agentuna:begin/end --> stays byte-identical, and a buffer that would rewrite marker lines returns Err(HandEditInsideMarkers{line}) with no write.
External edit after open then save returns Err(Conflict) with a `similar` unified diff and leaves the disk file untouched.
Successful save preserves the original file mode and does not add or remove a trailing newline.
Save to a read-only file returns Err(PermissionDenied{path,os_error}) with no partial write, and the watcher does not report the file back as drift.
notes: Decision 13: TA-011 owns managed-block rendering, TA-012 only supplies content.

title: New rule file intent and creation
description: Creates a rule file for a chosen type (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.local.md) at a chosen scope using that scope's verified path. The intent returns the resolved path, the template body (heading plus empty body, no trailing spaces) and a ChangeSet with a create-only op. Existing paths are a hard conflict per the refuse-to-overwrite rule.
acceptance: new_rule(ClaudeLocal, Project) resolves to <project>/CLAUDE.local.md and marks it as local-only (never staged for git).
Creating at a path that already exists returns Err(AlreadyExists{path}) and writes nothing.
Created file contains a single H1 with the file type name and ends with exactly one newline.
Global type creation returns Err(ReadOnly) when the Global store is not writable, with the resolved path in the message.
Successful creation returns the new RuleSource and the UI can open it in the editor without a rescan.
notes: Dialog UI is TA-057.

title: Per-agent deployment mode setting (link vs copy)
description: Adds the per-agent deployment mode: Link (default) or Copy, persisted in TF-023 settings under `link_mode.<agent>` (decision 18). Copy exists for tools that do not follow symlinks. Changing the setting edits future deployments only and offers a non-blocking migration count of already-linked items.
acceptance: Default for known agents is Link; default for agents created as custom is Copy. The stored key is exactly `link_mode.<agent>` (no `agent.<id>.deployment_mode` key exists).
set_link_mode(agent, Copy) persists through TF-023, survives restart, and is returned by agent_settings(); an unknown value is rejected at parse time and leaves the previous value intact.
Planning a deploy after switching to Copy emits copy ops and no symlink ops (assert op kinds in the ChangeSet).
Switching mode does not rewrite existing deployments; the returned MigrationOffer reports how many targets are currently links.
The setting change is recorded in the operations log with old and new values and no file writes.
notes: Decision 18: settings keys owned by TF-023. Reference: skillsmanager.md idea 8. UI control lives in TA-058.

title: Deployment planner honoring mode with symlink fallback
description: at-engine::deploy::plan turns (item, agent, scope, mode) into a concrete operation: symlink to the store source, or recursive copy with content hashing. When the filesystem rejects a symlink (EPERM, EXDEV, network volume) the planner falls back to copy, records a Warning::SymlinkUnsupported and continues; it never half-writes. Unmanaged destinations are refused with Adopt/MoveAside options. When the destination folder is read by more than one agent (TA-020 shared_roots), the plan reports the coupled agents so neither the ChangeSet preview nor the per-agent cell implies independent control.
acceptance: Mode=Link emits one Symlink op with source=store path and dest=agent path; mode=Copy emits one CopyTree op carrying the source tree hash.
Agents with managed=false are skipped: they appear in ChangeSet.skipped_unmanaged and produce zero ops, even when explicitly selected by a preset (source: TA-040 set_agent_managed).

Shared folder: enabling a skill for codex into <project>/.agents/skills emits coupled_agents=[omp] (and the reverse for omp), adds Warning::SharedRoot{path, agents}, and the preview / per-agent cell renders 'shared with omp' instead of an independent toggle.
Simulated EPERM on symlink produces a CopyTree op plus Warning::SymlinkUnsupported and still succeeds end to end.

Destination already occupied by an unmanaged folder returns Err(NativeConflict{path}) with zero ops (TF-005); after apply the deployment row records the mode actually used so the health line can report fallbacks.
notes: Skill folder content is produced by the Skills slice; this story owns destination choice and mode semantics.

title: Instruction composition order and local override semantics
description: Rules do not merge by name; they compose. at-engine::rules::compose(agent, scope) returns the ordered list of rule sources an agent actually reads: Global, then User, then Project, then Local, with agent-specific files (CLAUDE.md + CLAUDE.local.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md for Codex/omp) placed per agent behaviour. Effective config's Instructions tab renders this order with a scope badge per row and marks CLAUDE.local.md as an override rather than a replacement.
acceptance: compose(ClaudeCode, Project) returns Global CLAUDE.md, User CLAUDE.md, Project CLAUDE.md, Local CLAUDE.local.md in that order, each with its real path.
Missing layers are skipped and do not create placeholder rows.
A Local file never removes a Project file from the composition; it is marked override=true.
compose(Codex, Project) excludes CLAUDE.md and includes AGENTS.md only; an agent with no rule support returns an empty list plus Diagnostic::Unsupported.
Ordering is stable across runs and independent of filesystem readdir order (sorted tiebreak by path).
notes: Composition feeds both the Effective config Instructions tab and S-053's render targets.

title: AgentAdapter trait and registry
description: Defines the object-safe trait every adapter implements in at-adapters and the in-process registry that maps AgentId -> Arc<dyn AgentAdapter>. Methods: id(), capabilities(), detect(env), probe_version(), paths(scope, project), shared_roots(scope, project), list_native(), ensure_dirs(), read_io(kind, scope, project), render_io(deployment), write_io(plan), validate(). The trait covers skills folders, rule files and per-agent settings files. MCP server document read/write/merge is NOT implemented in at-adapters: read_io/render_io/write_io for ItemKind::McpServers MUST delegate to the TM-slice adapters (TM-005 claude_code, TM-006 codex, TM-007 omp, TM-008 capability matrix + generic JSON/TOML engine). Capabilities report what the delegated MCP layer supports. Errors are typed AgentError: NotInstalled, Parse{path,line,col}, Permission{path}, Unsupported{kind}, Conflict{path}, Delegate{source}. Registry also computes shared_roots(scope, project): a map from canonical destination folder to the set of agents that read it, so a folder loaded by several agents (codex and omp both read <project>/.agents/skills; codex also reads ~/.agents/skills) is never treated as per-agent private.
acceptance: Trait is Send+Sync and usable as Arc<dyn AgentAdapter>; registry.get(AgentId::ClaudeCode) returns the same instance across calls, all five adapters register through one `register()`, and tests/adapter_contract.rs runs detect/skills-read/skills-write/rules-read/rules-render/no-op for every registered adapter.

Every MCP read/write call made through the trait is forwarded to the TM adapter registered for that agent; a mock TM adapter records the call and at-adapters parses no mcpServers document itself (test asserts zero direct parse).
Capabilities delegate: MCP formats come from TM-008, while skills/folder and rules/markdown support is declared locally; claude_code reports supports_symlink=true, a custom agent can declare false.

shared_roots(Project, project) maps <project>/.agents/skills to {codex, omp}, ~/.agents/skills to {codex}, and every other skills root to exactly one agent; paths are canonicalized (realpath + case-fold on macOS) so two spellings of the same folder collapse into one entry.
Every adapter error carries the absolute path (and 1-based line/col for Parse); an Unsupported kind surfaces as a disabled toggle in the UI model, not a panic.
notes: TC-006 native scanner consumes this trait; registry is in-process, persistence of agent rows is TA-040.

title: Claude Code adapter: detection, skills, rules, settings.local.json
description: Owns everything Claude Code-specific except MCP document editing: binary/app detection and `<claude> --version`, skills roots ~/.claude/skills (User) and <project>/.claude/skills (Project), rule files CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md per scope, and .claude/settings.local.json for per-project enabled/disabled MCP server lists and permissions (span-patched, unknown keys preserved). Top-level `mcpServers` and projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers in ~/.claude.json are only enumerated as native metadata for the scanner; their read/write/merge is delegated to TM-005.
acceptance: detect() finds the `claude` binary and config root on this Mac and returns a parsed semver; a missing binary but existing ~/.claude yields ConfiguredOnly.

Skills: User/Project root is ~/.claude/skills / <project>/.claude/skills; Local deploys to <project>/.claude/skills/<slug> and AgenTuna adds that path to .git/info/exclude exactly once (idempotent, no duplicate line). Symlinked entries report link_target and an unmanaged folder is never overwritten.
Rule paths resolve to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, <project>/CLAUDE.md and <project>/CLAUDE.local.md; a lowercase claude.md is still discovered.
Patching .claude/settings.local.json preserves every unrelated key (permissions, hooks) byte for byte and changes only enabledMcpjsonServers/disabledMcpjsonServers entries.
Any McpServers read or write through this adapter is delegated to TM-005, verified by a mock that captures the document path (top-level vs projects[path]) and options.
notes: Live shape verified 2026-11-04: 19 project entries with enabledMcpjsonServers/disabledMcpjsonServers; MCP patching is TM-005's job.

title: Claude Code adapter golden-file tests (skills, rules, settings)
description: Fixture corpus under tests/fixtures/agents/claude_code/{settings,skills,rules,malformed,delegate}. Asserts settings.local.json round-trips, skills symlink listing, rule discovery and the MCP delegation boundary. ~/.claude.json MCP golden files belong to TM-005 and are not duplicated here.
acceptance: noop: read then render of a settings.local.json fixture with permissions/hooks keys is byte-identical (sha256 equal).
insert/remove: toggling one entry in enabledMcpjsonServers produces exactly one hunk and valid JSON; all other keys untouched.
skills: a fixture tree of symlinked skill folders reports each link_target and never resolves outside the fixture root.
delegate: an McpServers read through the adapter calls the TM-005 mock exactly once with the expected file path and returns the mock's document verbatim.
malformed: truncated settings.local.json yields Err(Parse{line,col}) and the file is unchanged.
notes: MCP-span golden files for ~/.claude.json live in the TM slice.

title: Codex adapter: detection, dual skills roots, AGENTS.md, config presence
description: Owns Codex detection (`codex --version`), config root ~/.codex, skills root resolution across ~/.codex/skills and ~/.agents/skills (shared with other tools), project rules AGENTS.md and user ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, and read-only enumeration of [projects."<path>"] trust tables for the native scanner. [mcp_servers.*] reads, writes, enabled=false toggles and comment-preserving TOML patches are delegated to TM-006.
acceptance: detect() returns Installed with a parsed version on this Mac and records the config root ~/.codex.

Skills: user roots remain ~/.codex/skills and ~/.agents/skills; Local deploys to <project>/.agents/skills/<slug>, adds that path to .git/info/exclude once, and the alternative root stays unmanaged_alternative.
Rule paths resolve to ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and <project>/AGENTS.md; a project without AGENTS.md returns an empty rule list plus FileMissing diagnostic.
Reading [projects.*] trust tables never mutates config.toml and returns project path + trust_level only (no other keys exposed).
Any [mcp_servers] read/write is delegated to TM-006; the adapter performs no MCP parse itself (test asserts delegation and unchanged config hash for skills/rules writes).
notes: MCP TOML editing and comment preservation are TM-006 acceptance criteria, not duplicated here.

title: Codex adapter golden-file tests (skills, rules, config presence)
description: Fixtures for skill-root selection, AGENTS.md create/edit, read-only [projects.*] parsing, and MCP delegation. TOML MCP golden files are owned by TM-006.
acceptance: skills-root fixture where both ~/.codex/skills and ~/.agents/skills exist resolves to the configured primary and lists the alternative as exists=true.
AGENTS.md create writes one trailing newline and preserves existing body content outside the managed block.

A config.toml fixture with 10 [projects.*] tables and 5 [mcp_servers.*] tables yields all project paths and delegates the server list to the TM-006 mock, whose file hash stays unchanged after a skills-only operation.
malformed AGENTS.md (invalid UTF-8) yields Err(Parse{path}) and no write.
MCP enable/disable through the adapter records a single delegation call with enabled=false and performs no local TOML write.

title: omp adapter: detection, managed-skills vs skills, AGENTS.md
description: Owns omp detection (binary `omp`, ~/.omp/agent root), skills root resolution managed-skills first then skills, and AGENTS.md rule files. The absence of ~/.omp/agent/skills on this Mac must not be treated as an error. `mcpServers` in ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json is enumerated as native metadata only; read/write is delegated to TM-007.
acceptance: detect() on this Mac returns Installed with a version and config root ~/.omp/agent.

Skills: user roots stay managed-skills then skills; Local deploys to <project>/.agents/skills/<slug> (omp walks up to `.agents/skills`, with `.agent/skills` accepted on read), and AgenTuna adds the deployed path to .git/info/exclude exactly once.
Skills listing ignores .bak-* siblings (this Mac has mcp.json.bak-*) and other non-directory entries; ~/.omp/agent/skills may legitimately not exist.
AGENTS.md resolves at project root and any configured user-level path; missing user-level file is not an error.
McpServers calls delegate to TM-007 with the path ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json; the adapter itself performs no JSON mutation of that file.
notes: omp binary confirms project skill loading from .agent/skills and .agents/skills (project walk-up); managed-skills remains the user-level managed root. Corrects research/skillsmanager.md, Corrections.

title: omp adapter golden-file tests (skills, rules, delegation)
description: Fixtures for the managed-skills/skills dual tree, $schema-bearing mcp.json metadata, AGENTS.md, and delegation to TM-007.
acceptance: managed-skills-only fixture reports managed root with N skills and skills root exists=false.
skills scan never descends into mcp.json, .bak files or blobs/ and returns only directories containing SKILL.md.
AGENTS.md create/edit round-trips with one trailing newline and preserves user text outside the managed block.
An McpServers read through the adapter is served by the TM-007 mock and the on-disk mcp.json hash is unchanged.
Deleted managed-skills directory during a session flips to NeedsPath on the next scan without panicking.

title: Cursor adapter: detection, skills, .mdc rules, MCP path exposure
description: Cursor is not installed on this Mac, so the adapter works from declared candidates. Owns detection (~/.cursor, Cursor.app, `cursor` binary), skills roots ~/.cursor/skills and <project>/.cursor/skills, rule files .cursor/rules/*.mdc with YAML frontmatter (description, globs, alwaysApply), and exposure of the mcp.json paths (~/.cursor/mcp.json, <project>/.cursor/mcp.json). MCP document read/write is delegated to TM-008's generic JSON engine.
acceptance: detect() on this Mac (no ~/.cursor/skills, ~/.cursor exists with unrelated content) returns ConfiguredOnly with candidates listed and never reports skills as available.
Skills: user/project roots are ~/.cursor/skills and <project>/.cursor/skills; Local deploys to <project>/.cursor/skills/<slug> and AgenTuna adds that path to .git/info/exclude exactly once.
Writing a .mdc rule emits frontmatter with description/globs/alwaysApply in that order and a blank line before the body; malformed frontmatter yields Err(Parse{line,col}).
Rule discovery lists existing .mdc files with parsed frontmatter; a missing skills root returns an empty list plus FileMissing diagnostic, not an error.
McpServers calls delegate to TM-008 with the resolved cursor path; a custom agent_paths override changes that path for both detection and delegation.
notes: Cursor format is unverified on this machine; fixtures are synthetic and must be re-checked when Cursor is installed.

title: Cursor adapter golden-file tests (skills, .mdc, delegation)
description: Synthetic fixtures for .cursor/skills trees, .cursor/rules/*.mdc and the delegation boundary to TM-008.
acceptance: Skills noop scan on a two-skill fixture returns both with name and path, no writes.
.mdc frontmatter round-trips with globs as a list and alwaysApply boolean untouched.
NotInstalled detection produces zero writes for every attempted operation (assert empty change set).
MCP read through the adapter records one TM-008 delegation call and leaves the fixture hash unchanged.
Malformed .mdc frontmatter yields Err(Parse{line,col}) with the file path.

title: Custom agent adapter defined by folder
description: One generic adapter instance per custom agent registry row. A CustomAgentSpec declares display name, root folder, skills subfolder, mcp file path plus format (json|toml|none), rule file names, and supports_symlink. Skills and rules use the shared at-adapters code; MCP documents go through TM-008's generic JSON/TOML engine so no new parser is added.
acceptance: A spec pointing at ~/.mytool with skills/, mcp.json (json) and RULES.md is detected, listed and written through the same code path as built-ins; Local deploys to <project>/<spec.skills_subfolder>/<slug> and adds that path to .git/info/exclude once.
MCP read/write is delegated to TM-008 with (path, format); format=none returns Unsupported without touching disk.
Invalid spec (relative root, root '/', missing root) is rejected at registry validation with a specific error and never instantiates an adapter.
supports_symlink=false forces copy deployments and is reported in capabilities.
Adding a spec and rescanning makes the agent appear in the effective config agent filter without restart (in-process registry refresh).
notes: UI creation is TA-060; reference: skillsmanager.md idea 10 (custom agents by folder).

title: Custom agent adapter golden-file tests (skills, rules, delegation)
description: Fixtures for the generic adapter: a JSON-format and a TOML-format spec, a spec with no MCP file, and a spec pointing at a deleted folder.
acceptance: Skills and rules read/noop on the JSON fixture produce zero writes and identical listings across two scans.
TOML-format spec delegates MCP operations to TM-008 with format=toml and the adapter performs no parse of its own.
format=none returns Unsupported for MCP read/write and still lists skills and rules.
Deleted root folder during a session produces Err(NotInstalled) on the next read with the last known path in the message.
Rule file names are matched case-insensitively on macOS and the on-disk name is preserved.

title: Agent detection and version probing orchestrator
description: at-adapters::detect runs all adapters concurrently: PATH lookup of the CLI binary, well-known app-bundle paths on macOS, config-root existence, and any user path override. Version is probed by running `<bin> --version` with a 2s timeout and parsing the first semver triple. Result is Detection { Installed{version, binary, config_root}, ConfiguredOnly{config_root}, NotInstalled{candidates} }, cached in the agents table with checked_at.
acceptance: On this Mac, claude_code, codex and omp report Installed with a parsed version; cursor reports ConfiguredOnly or NotInstalled but never Installed without a skills root.
A binary that exits non-zero or prints garbage yields Installed{version: Unknown} rather than NotInstalled.
A hung `--version` is killed at 2s and does not block the batch; total cold detection of 5 adapters finishes in under 3s.
Results are written to the agents table and reused within the TTL (default 10 min) unless a rescan is forced.
Detection never shells out from a synchronous command or the webview; it is a tokio task whose result arrives as a Tauri event through the app bridge.
notes: CLI names: claude, codex, omp, cursor. Version flags may need per-adapter fallbacks (e.g. --version vs version).

title: Verified agent path resolution and overrides
description: Each adapter publishes ordered candidate paths per kind and scope per X10; at-adapters::paths verifies them with stat and read access, records verified=true only for usable targets, and prefers an agent_paths override. Unverified or vanished paths raise NeedsPath with the candidate list, which drives the Connect/Set path dialog. No single path is hard-coded as the only option.
acceptance: claude_code candidates for User skills are [~/.claude/skills]; a missing folder is reported NeedsPath with that candidate, not an error.
codex skills candidates are [~/.codex/skills, ~/.agents/skills]; the first verified one wins and the other is retained as alternative.
omp skills candidates are [~/.omp/agent/managed-skills, ~/.omp/agent/skills]; on this Mac the first verifies and the second stays exists=false.
An override saved by the user is used verbatim and skipped candidate probing; the override is recorded with verified=true only after a successful stat.
A path that disappears after verification flips to NeedsPath on the next scan and preserves the last known path for display.
notes: Path cheap-lists come from X10 and live file checks; keep the table in one place per adapter.

title: agents and agent_paths repositories over TF-011 tables
description: Repository layer only (decision 8: no DDL). at-db reads and writes the `agents` and `agent_paths` tables created by TF-011, exposing upsert_agent, set_agent_managed, set_path_override, list_agents_on_mac and settings accessors. Managed state (let AgenTuna manage this agent) is a first-class column so deployment and detection can skip unmanaged agents.
acceptance: Repository operates on the TF-011 schema unchanged; this story adds no migrations and the schema_version does not advance.
upsert_agent is idempotent by id and never duplicates the 4 built-in agents after repeated detection cycles.
set_agent_managed(agent, false) persists, is returned by list_agents_on_mac, and a subsequent deploy or detection pass skips that agent.
set_path_override stores verified=false until the probe succeeds, then flips it and keeps is_override=1.
list_agents_on_mac returns installed agents first, then ConfiguredOnly, then NotInstalled, each with its resolved primary path and managed flag.
notes: Table DDL is TF-011 per decision 8. Built-in slugs: claude_code, codex, omp, cursor.

title: deployments and locks repositories and queries over TF-013/TF-014
description: Read/write repository plus query layer over the `deployments` and `locks` tables owned by TF-013 and TF-014 (no DDL here). Provides effective_rows(scope, agent), health_counts(agent_id) -> managed/in_sync/total, and lock lookup by item and scope.
acceptance: No migrations are added; all columns/constraints come from TF-013 and TF-014.
upsert_deployment updates state/mode/hashes in place for the same (item, agent, scope, project) and refreshes updated_at.
health_counts returns managed = count(state != Native), in_sync = count(state = Linked AND sync = InSync), total = count(*), and excludes deployments of unmanaged agents from the health line counts.
effective_rows filters by scope and agent and returns rows joined with item kind and name in a single prepared statement (no N+1).
A query for an unknown agent returns zero counts rather than an error.
notes: Health counts feed TA-033 and the Agents page cards.

title: Overview queries: scope counts, last edited, recent changes
description: SQL layer for TA-009: counts per scope per kind from items/deployments, lock counts from locks, last_edited from operations joined with operation_files, and recent_changes (limit N) with operation id, kind, summary, created_at and file count. Needs-attention candidate queries: failing health checks, drift events, native deployments, missing agents.
acceptance: counts_for_scope returns skills/mcp/rules/locks in one query and is correct on a seeded fixture with 12 items across 3 scopes.
last_edited returns the max operations.created_at per scope and NULL when no operations exist.
recent_changes with limit=20 returns at most 20 rows ordered created_at desc, id desc for ties.
All overview queries together run in < 50 ms on a fixture with 10k operations rows.
Queries are read-only and do not hold a write transaction while the UI renders.
notes: Operations log ownership is TF-009; this story only reads it.

title: Rules index projection in items and item_versions
description: Stores discovered rule files as items with kind='rule' plus item_versions rows keyed by (item_id, scope, path) holding sha256, bytes, mtime and last_seen. Provides upsert_on_scan, rules_for_scope, and duplicate detection when the same real path is reachable through a symlink and its target.
acceptance: Scanning 3 rule files inserts 3 items and 3 item_versions rows; rescanning unchanged files updates last_seen only and keeps the same item ids.
A symlink and its target both discovered resolve to one row with link_target recorded, not two.
rules_for_scope returns rows ordered by agent then file name, with managed flag and link_target.
Deleted file removal marks the item missing (state column) instead of deleting history.
Concurrent upsert from watcher and manual rescan does not duplicate rows (INSERT OR REPLACE by natural key).

title: Overview screen shell and Project scope variant
description: ui/src/screens/overview renders the Project Overview: three scope cards (Project highlighted), effective summary bar with per-scope proportions, Needs attention list and Recent changes timeline. Consumes the TA-009 payload through the app bridge. Uses TU-002 (cards, badges, status dot), TU-005 (toasts) and TU-004 (row menus).
acceptance: Populated: cards show skill/server/rule counts, lock count and last-edited relative time; summary bar segments sum to 100% and show percentage labels.
Empty: a scope with no store renders an empty card with a 'Set up this scope' action and no counts of zero as a fake success.
Loading: skeleton cards render while the overview job is in flight; no layout jump when data arrives.
Error: a failed job renders an inline error row with the message and a Retry button that re-runs the job.
Every Needs attention row click navigates to its NavigationTarget (screen + filter) without a full reload.
notes: Module names follow CONTRACT.md: ui/src/screens/overview.

title: Overview User and Global variants with locks and admin state
description: Same overview module, different scope: the User variant shows user store path and per-agent install summary; the Global variant shows the admin store path, a read-only banner when Global is not writable, and lock counts with a padlocked card. Locked item rows show a padlock and a tooltip with the lock reason.
acceptance: Global scope with a non-writable store renders the read-only banner plus an 'Enable global writes' action and still lists locks read from the `locks` table.
Global scope with writable store hides the banner; lock count equals the locks table count for scope=Global.
User variant omits the admin banner and shows the resolved ~/.agentuna path with a copy button.
Switching scope via the top bar remounts the variant within one frame and preserves scroll position per scope.
A lock with a missing item appears in the card's lock count and as a Needs attention row 'Locked item not found'.
notes: Admin/privilege state comes from TA-080's GlobalStoreStatus.

title: Needs attention and Recent changes components
description: Two reusable widgets in ui/src/screens/overview: attention_list(entries) with severity icon, title, subtitle and jump action; changes_timeline(entries) with operation summary, relative time, scope badge and file count expandable to the file list. Both consume TA-009 view models and have explicit empty states.
acceptance: attention_list renders at most 5 rows per severity class with a 'Show all N' expansion; clicking a row emits NavigationTarget.
changes_timeline groups items under Today/Yesterday/Earlier headers using local time and shows 'No changes yet' when empty.
A drift entry renders a warning dot; a failing health entry renders a red dot; colors come from TU-001 tokens only.
Expanding an operation row lists its touched files with per-file scope badges without a second network/DB call (payload already includes them).
Rows are keyboard-focusable and Enter activates the same action as click (accessibility parity with O14).

title: Scope state, routing and persistence (switcher wiring)
description: Owns the selected scope in ui/src/state (TU-009), routes every screen to the matching scope view, persists the last scope per project in settings, and mounts the TU-040 switcher widget in the TU-006 top bar. Shortcuts are Cmd+Shift+1/2/3/4 for Global/User/Project/Local (decision 11); the widget itself only renders and emits selection events.
acceptance: Selecting Global/User/Project switches routing and filters on every screen; Local selection is available when the project has a local root and opens Effective config filtered to Local.
Cmd+Shift+1/2/3/4 select Global/User/Project/Local and the TU-040 widget reflects the change within one frame; no Cmd+1..3 binding for scopes exists (those are screen shortcuts owned by TU-016).
Selection is persisted per project in TF-023 settings under `last_scope.<project_id>` and restored on next launch of that project.
Global selection is disabled with tooltip 'Global store not available' when GlobalStoreStatus is Unavailable.
The story owns state and routing only; all rendering, a11y roles and snapshots of the control live in TU-040.
notes: Decision 11: TU-040 is the widget, TA-053 is the behaviour.

title: Effective config screen
description: ui/src/screens/effective renders tabs Skills / MCP servers / Instructions over the TA-006 query. Each row shows name, source scope badge, agent count, state badge and a per-agent file list expander. A 'Disabled here' section lists tombstones with reason. Change-for-this-repo actions live in the row menu and call TA-008 intents behind a confirm.
acceptance: Populated: selecting the MCP tab lists resolved servers with source scope and agent count; expanding a row lists each agent's target file path and state.
Disabled here: rows show the tombstone path and the suppressed scope, with a 'Re-enable' action that restores the item.
Empty: a scope with no items shows 'Nothing configured at this scope' plus a link to the inherited scope with items.
Loading and error states match the shell pattern (skeletons, inline error with Retry) and the tab selection survives a reload.
Disable in this repo / Override in Project / Edit User definition are offered exactly when the engine says they are allowed (locked rows hide them and show the lock reason).
notes: Diff preview before apply uses TU-007.

title: Why-is-this-on overlay
description: An overlay (TU-004) rendering the TA-007 trace: one row per scope with a connecting rail, state chip, file path with line number, and the winning row highlighted. Header states the verdict ('On, from User'), footer actions: Open file, Copy path, Open in Effective config. Reachable from the Effective config row menu, the MCP detail screen and the command palette.
acceptance: Rendering a trace with 4 steps shows every scope row including Absent ones (dimmed) so the chain is legible; the winning row is visually distinct.
Verdict header reads either 'On, from <scope>' or 'Off, <reason>' matching the decisive step; unknown/unreadable steps render with an error chip and the OS message.
Open file launches the OS editor at the recorded path (no line jump required); Copy path copies the absolute path and shows a toast.
Overlay closes on Esc and on backdrop click, and focus returns to the invoking row.
Works for skills, MCP servers and rules; a rule trace lists composed sources rather than a single winner.
notes: O06 menu entry 'Why is this on?' is owned by the MCP slice; this story provides the overlay.

title: Instructions screen: scope file list, editor, preview, save/discard
description: ui/src/screens/instructions shows a left list of rule files grouped by scope with a managed/native badge, and a right pane with the TU-008 editor (line numbers, markdown syntax highlighting). Toolbar: Edit/Preview toggle (react-markdown with a sanitizer), unsaved-changes dot, Save (Cmd+S) and Discard. Save goes through TA-012; conflicts open a reload/overwrite prompt.
acceptance: Populated: selecting CLAUDE.md at Project loads its content, shows the scope badge and marks the file clean; editing sets the dirty dot and enables Save/Discard.
Preview renders headings, lists, code fences and links; switching back preserves the buffer and caret.
Cmd+S saves, clears the dirty dot, emits a success toast, and refuses to close the screen with unsaved changes without a confirm.
Conflict: external edit detected on save shows a dialog with the unified diff and Reload / Overwrite choices; Overwrite performs a forced save with a backup.
Empty/error: no rule files at the scope shows the New rule action; unreadable file renders an inline permission error with the path.
notes: Markdown preview uses react-markdown with a sanitizer per CONTRACT stack.

title: New rule file dialog
description: Modal (TU-004) with file-type radio cards (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.local.md), scope radio cards, a read-only target path preview and a Create action wired to TA-013. Shows an inline conflict when the path exists, and disables Global when read-only.
acceptance: Changing type or scope updates the target path preview immediately from the adapter path table.
Create on an existing path shows 'File already exists' with the path and keeps the dialog open; no write occurs.
Successful create closes the dialog, emits a toast, opens the new file in the Instructions editor and refreshes the file list.
Global option is disabled with the read-only reason when Global is not writable; Local option is disabled when the project is not a git repo.
Esc/Cancel writes nothing and restores focus to the invoking Add menu item.
notes: Add menu O03 is TU-owned; this story is the dialog.

title: Agents screen: cards, health line, manage toggle, copy/link setting
description: ui/src/screens/agents renders one card per agent: icon, name, installed version, config paths, native format, managed counts, items outside AgenTuna, the one-line health summary, a Let AgenTuna manage this agent toggle, a deployment mode control (Link/Copy) and per-agent Rescan. Missing agents render a Set path action.
acceptance: Health line renders exactly 'path · N / N managed · N in sync' using TA-033 output; a fallback to copy is appended as '· copy fallback' when any deployment recorded a symlink failure.
Managed counts and 'items outside AgenTuna' come from deployments/native counts and are correct on a seeded fixture (3 managed, 2 native).
Toggling manage off stops rendering and writing for that agent but leaves existing files on disk; toggling on triggers a rescan and shows affected file counts.
Deployment mode segmented control persists via TA-014 and shows the migration offer count when switching Link->Copy with existing links.
States: NotInstalled shows Set path; ConfiguredOnly shows 'Found config, CLI missing'; detection in flight shows a skeleton card; a failed rescan shows an inline error with Retry.
notes: Depends on TA-033 health line; keep counts read-only here.

title: Connect agent / Set path dialog
description: Modal from the Agents card and from the command palette: shows the agent's candidate paths with existence results, a path input with Browse (native file dialog), validation on change (exists, is directory, looks like the expected tool by finding a skills subfolder or config file) and Save disabled until valid. Saving writes an agent_paths override and re-runs detection.
acceptance: Opening for Cursor lists candidates from TA-032 with exists=false markers and focuses the path input.
Typing a path that exists but has no expected structure shows a warning (not a hard block) 'No skills folder or config file found here'.
Browse opens the OS directory picker and fills the input; invalid paths keep Save disabled with a reason under the field.
Save persists the override, flips detection to Installed, closes the dialog, toasts, and the card updates without restart.
Cancel/Esc writes nothing; reopening shows the previously saved override prefilled.
notes: Native picker crate is not fixed by the contract; call rfd from a Rust command (never grant a dialog or fs capability to the webview) and note in code.

title: Add custom agent dialog
description: Modal that builds a CustomAgentSpec: display name, root folder (Browse), optional skills subfolder, MCP file path plus format select (JSON / TOML / none), rule file names (comma list), supports-symlink checkbox, then Save. Validation mirrors TA-029 registry rules and previews the resolved paths before saving.
acceptance: Saving a valid spec creates the registry row, instantiates the adapter, rescans and shows the new agent card without restart.
Relative or '/' root is rejected inline with a specific message and Save stays disabled.
Format=none hides the MCP path field and the resulting card shows 'MCP not supported'.
Path preview shows resolved absolute paths for skills/MCP/rules before saving.
Duplicate display name is rejected with 'An agent with this name exists' and offers to open the existing card.

title: Per-agent health line computation
description: at-engine::health::line(agent_id) composes the one-line summary shown on the Agents card: primary path relative to HOME (~-shortened), managed/total counts of items AgenTuna owns for that agent, count in sync, plus a copy-fallback suffix when a deployment fell back from symlink. Managed means the deployment row exists and state != Native; in sync means Linked + InSync.
acceptance: Returns the exact format '~/.claude/skills · 7 / 9 managed · 8 in sync' with a single middle-dot separator and spaces around '/'.
When an agent has no deployments it returns '<path> · 0 / 0 managed · 0 in sync' and the UI renders a 'nothing deployed' hint instead of the counts.
A deployment recorded with mode=copy after a symlink failure adds ' · copy fallback'; a healthy copy-only agent (custom with supports_symlink=false) does not.
Counts are recomputed after any deploy/undeploy operation and the value is stable across two consecutive calls with no changes.
An agent whose primary path is unverified returns the last known path with a leading '!' marker and a NeedsPath diagnostic.
notes: Format taken from skillsmanager.md idea 5; agents page renders it verbatim.

title: CLI: agents, effective and why commands with --json
description: at-cli registers the noun-first command groups `agents`, `effective`, `why`, `overview` and `rules` on the TU-026 CLI command tree (clap derive, shared with the rest of the binary). Subcommands: `agents list`, `agents inspect <id>`, `effective --scope <s> [--agent <id>] [--kind <k>]`, `why <item> --scope <s> [--agent <id>]`. All support --json emitting the TU-033 JSON envelope with the same payload structs the GUI uses. Human output is a compact table; diagnostics go to stderr. The `effective` group is also the extension point for `effective lock` / `effective unlock` delivered by TA-097.
acceptance: `agentuna agents list --json` wraps its array in the TU-033 envelope and the payload carries id, installed, version, primary_path and health_line for each agent.
`agentuna effective --scope project --kind mcp --json` returns items plus disabled_here arrays matching TA-006 output inside the same TU-033 envelope.
`agentuna why <id> --scope project --json` emits the 4-step trace with line numbers and verdict inside the TU-033 envelope.
Exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime/engine error, 2 usage error; --json mode never writes non-JSON to stdout and the envelope is byte-stable across runs.
The five groups are registered on the TU-026 tree and appear in `--help` exactly once; `effective lock|unlock` subcommands are added by TA-097 without re-registering the group.
notes: Agent-operable CLI is X11 idea 3; TU-026 owns the CLI tree and TU-033 the JSON envelope, this story owns these five groups.

title: CLI: overview and rules commands
description: Registers `overview` and `rules` alongside the TA-070 groups on the TU-026 command tree: `agentuna overview --scope <s> --json`, `rules list --scope <s>`, `rules show <path>`, `rules save <path> --stdin [--force]`, `rules new --type <t> --scope <s>`. All --json output uses the TU-033 envelope. Save reads the buffer from stdin, enforces the concurrency check unless --force, and prints the resulting diff summary.
acceptance: `overview --scope user --json` returns the same payload the Overview screen renders, including needs_attention and recent_changes, inside the TU-033 envelope.
`rules show` prints raw file bytes with no ANSI decoration when piped; `rules list --json` returns scope, path, managed, size and hash inside the envelope.
`rules save --stdin` with an unchanged buffer exits 0 and writes nothing; with an externally modified file exits 1 with a conflict diff and no write.
`rules save --stdin --force` writes through the backup pipeline and prints the Backup path.
`rules new --type AGENTS.md --scope project` fails with exit 1 and 'already exists' when the file is present; both groups appear once in the TU-026 `--help` tree.
notes: Rules subcommands are the agent-operable surface for F13; TU-033 owns envelope shape.

title: Global store path and admin/privilege handling for writes
description: Reads the Global store location from TF-022 AppPaths (decision 2: default `/Library/Application Support/AgenTuna/global`, override `AGENTUNA_GLOBAL_STORE`, then settings key `global_store_path`), reports GlobalStoreStatus {Available, ReadOnly, Unavailable} with the reason, and performs privileged writes only through an explicit one-shot authorization prompt (macOS Authorization Services / osascript with administrator privileges) that the user confirms. AgenTuna never runs a silent sudo and never partly writes a file. Locks are read from the `locks` table, never from the Global store.
acceptance: The path is never hard-coded: with AGENTUNA_GLOBAL_STORE set, AppPaths returns that path and the Global card shows it; with the settings key set and no env var, the settings value wins over the default.

When the resolved directory is absent, status is Unavailable with the checked path; when it exists but is not writable, status is ReadOnly and every Global intent returns Err(ReadOnly) before any temp file is created.
The 'Enable global writes' action runs one privileged copy/chown, prompts the OS dialog, and on cancel leaves status ReadOnly and writes nothing.
A writable temp dir supplied through AppPaths makes Global fully functional in tests without elevation.
Locks displayed and enforced at Global come from the `locks` table only; a lock row is visible even when the store is ReadOnly.
notes: No at-platform crate exists in CONTRACT.md; helper lives in at-app::platform over at-fs atomic primitives.

title: Detection loop: start scan, watcher-triggered rescan, self-write suppression
description: Wires TF-007 watchers over agent config roots (~/.claude.json, ~/.codex, ~/.omp/agent, ~/.cursor, project .claude/.agents/.agentuna) into a debounced rescan pipeline: 500 ms debounce, typed DetectionEvent to the UI via TF-008, own writes suppressed by path+hash for one event. A root that cannot be watched logs a Diagnostic and does not stop the others.
acceptance: Editing ~/.claude.json externally triggers exactly one rescan after the debounce window and the Agents/Effective views refresh without manual action.
Agents with managed=false are detected and shown but never rescanned into deployments or rewritten; the event is recorded as SkippedUnmanaged{agent}.
AgenTuna's own write to a watched file produces zero drift events (self-write suppression verified by event count).
A burst of 20 file events inside 500 ms collapses into one rescan, and a rescan is coalesced with an in-flight scan.
An unwatchable root emits Diagnostic::WatchFailed{path,os_error} and the remaining roots keep working.
notes: debounce config from notify-debouncer-full per CONTRACT stack.

title: Scope resolution matrix tests
description: Table-driven test suite covering the full matrix: 4 scopes x {absent, defined, shadowed, disabled, locked} x kind {skill, mcp} x agent {claude_code, codex, omp, cursor, custom}. Each case is a TOML/JSON fixture plus an expected resolution snapshot (winner, shadowed list, disabled list, state). Includes property tests for monotonicity of adding a deeper layer.
acceptance: All 40+ matrix rows pass with an expected-winner snapshot stored under tests/fixtures/resolution/.
Property: adding a definition at a deeper scope changes the winner only for that logical id, never for any other id.
Property: removing a tombstone at scope S restores the same winner that existed before the tombstone, byte-for-byte identical snapshot.
Lock rows dominate every other row in the matrix: no case with a lock yields a non-locked winner.
Skill name normalization cases (case, whitespace, NFC vs NFD, trailing dot) each map to one logical id and are asserted explicitly.
notes: Primary regression net for the whole slice.

title: Adapter golden-file harness: skills, rules and settings formats
description: A reusable harness (tests/adapter_golden.rs) that, for every registered adapter, walks tests/fixtures/agents/<agent>/<case>/ and asserts: input parses, no-op read→render is byte-identical, mutation output equals expected/after, both files re-parse, and no file outside the expected diff changed. MCP document fixtures are contributed by the TM slice through the same harness convention.
acceptance: Adding a new skills/rules/settings fixture folder requires no new test code; the harness picks it up by convention.
A deliberately wrong expected file fails with a readable unified diff naming the fixture and adapter.
Byte identity uses full-file bytes, not line-normalized text (CRLF and trailing-newline differences fail).

Coverage guard: the suite fails if a registered adapter has fewer than one noop, one insert, one remove and one malformed case for skills/rules/settings, and if its MCP path is not delegated to a TM adapter.
Runs against temp-copied fixtures so no test mutates the repository fixtures.
notes: Foundation for TA-022/024/026/028/030; TM slice can register its own fixtures with the same runner.

title: Adapter robustness: malformed settings, permissions, concurrency, symlinks
description: Negative-path suite over all adapters for the data at-adapters owns: truncated settings.local.json, BOM prefix, CRLF rules, invalid UTF-8 markdown, chmod 0444 target, unwritable directory, dangling symlink, symlink loop, and an external write between read and write (mtime+content change). MCP document corruption cases live in the TM suite.
acceptance: Every malformed fixture maps to AgentError::Parse with a 1-based line/col within the fixture's real error location.
chmod 0444 on a rule target yields PermissionDenied and the file bytes are unchanged (sha256 equal).
A file changed between read and write yields Conflict after one retry; the external content remains intact and no temp file is left in the directory.
Dangling symlink and symlink loop yield specific diagnostics and the scan continues with other items.
Invalid UTF-8 markdown is rejected with Parse and never lossily converted.
notes: MCP-format robustness is covered by TM-005..TM-008 tests.

title: Effective config and why-trace snapshot tests
description: Seeded-DB snapshot tests for TA-006 and TA-007 outputs: insta-style snapshots of the serialized EffectiveConfig and TraceStep vectors for fixture scenarios (inherited, shadowed, disabled, locked, native, missing agent, unreadable file).
acceptance: Each defined scenario has a committed snapshot; changing output without updating the snapshot fails the test.
Trace snapshots include line numbers, and a fixture moving the server down 3 lines changes only the line fields.
Locked scenario snapshot shows blocked steps and no winning step.
Unreadable-file scenario snapshot includes the OS error string field populated (not empty).
Snapshots are generated from a temp DB seeded by migrations, never from the developer's real ~/.agentuna.

title: Instructions render, composition and drift tests
description: Covers TA-010/011/016: discovery fixtures per scope, composition order per agent, managed-block render into both files, idempotent re-render, adopt-required and malformed-block refusals, and an external edit producing a drift event.
acceptance: Render to both files from one source yields identical managed-block bodies and one operations row; second render changes no bytes and no mtime.
Composition for Claude Code returns 4 ordered sources; for Codex returns only AGENTS.md sources; snapshots locked.
Unterminated managed block fixture returns MalformedManagedBlock with the correct line and neither file is written (hashes equal).
External edit outside the managed block is detected as drift and preserved on the next render.
New rule creation test asserts the file exists with one trailing newline and appears in the next scan.

title: Overview aggregate and health line tests
description: Seeded fixtures asserting TA-009 and TA-033 outputs: counts per scope, needs-attention ordering and caps, recent changes limit and ordering, empty-store behaviour, and health line formatting including copy-fallback suffix.
acceptance: Seeded fixture with 12 items produces exactly the expected counts per scope and kind (golden values).
Needs attention returns severity order Critical->Warning->Info and caps at 5 per class while exposing the true total.
Empty store returns zero counts and no error path (assert Ok, empty vectors).
Health line matches the exact expected string for: healthy, nothing deployed, copy fallback, unverified path.
Overview payload build on 10k operations stays under the 50 ms budget on CI hardware (soft assertion with printed timing).

title: Local scope end-to-end test with temp HOME and gitignore
description: Integration test using TF-010's temp HOME fixture plus a temp git repo: writes Local overrides, verifies precedence, gitignore idempotence, tombstone isolation between two projects that share the same User store, and that no Local file is ever staged.
acceptance: Local definition overrides Project and appears with scope=local in the effective payload.
.gitignore gains exactly one line after two ensure_gitignore calls; `git status --porcelain` shows no .agentuna/local entries.
Two temp repos with different Local tombstones resolve independently against the same User store.
Local-only project (not a git repo) still resolves with local layer flagged NotAvailable and does not error.
Deleting the local store directory restores pre-local winners with no stale DB rows (rescan reconciles).

title: Lock and unlock items at Global scope
description: Row action available in the Effective config screen and in the Skills/MCP row menus when the active scope is Global: Lock with a required reason, Unlock with confirmation. Uses the TA-002 engine lock API, the TU-004 dialog framework and the TU-005 toast service, and updates locked presentation (padlock, disabled lower-scope toggles with reason) after the engine returns. The same operations are exposed on the CLI as `effective lock <item> --reason <text>` and `effective unlock <item>` under the TA-070 `effective` group with TU-033 JSON envelope output.
acceptance: Action visibility: Lock appears only when the active scope is Global, the item is unlocked and the Global store is writable; on a read-only store it renders disabled with the ReadOnly reason. Unlock appears only for locked items.
Reason dialog: non-empty reason is required (max 200 chars); Cancel/Esc writes nothing and returns focus to the row.
After lock, the row shows a padlock, Effective config re-renders from a fresh query, and lower-scope toggles are disabled with the lock reason tooltip; a success toast names the item.

CLI: `agentuna effective lock <item> --reason "..." --json` and `effective unlock <item> --json` emit the TU-033 envelope with {locked, reason}; a locked-at-lower-scope denial exits 1 with the reason.
Failure path: an engine Err (ReadOnly, Locked, unknown item) shows a warning toast and leaves the row state unchanged (verified by comparing the rendered model before/after).
notes: CLI subcommands extend TA-070's `effective` group without re-registering it; engine semantics stay in TA-002.

title: Privileged Global write elevation tests
description: Test suite for TA-080's elevation path using TF-010's temp HOME fixture plus a injectable authorization runner: asserts cancel, deny, success and read-only states, and that no partial files, temp files or orphan backups survive a failed elevation.
acceptance: Cancel: authorization prompt dismissed → GlobalStoreStatus stays ReadOnly, zero bytes written and no temp file left in the resolved Global directory (directory listing identical before/after).
Deny: authorization rejected → Err(NotAuthorized) surfaced once, no retry loop, no writes, no operations row.
Success: writable target after elevation contains the expected file bytes and mode, status flips to Available, and exactly one operations row with the elevated files is recorded.
Read-only store: every Global intent returns Err(ReadOnly) before the authorization runner is invoked (assert runner call count 0).
A writable path supplied through AppPaths performs the same writes with the runner call count 0, proving tests and non-admin setups never require elevation.
notes: Authorization runner is injected behind a trait so CI never opens a real OS dialog.
